rationale:
The per-site imagery style guide is the platform's brand contract for generated images, and its most identity-bearing field — the palette — is being silently discarded before it reaches the model. composeDirection joins medium -> mood -> palette, so the palette is ALWAYS last, and composeImagePromptWithDirection then truncates the whole composed direction at maxImageryDirectionInPrompt = 200 chars. A verbose medium+mood therefore evicts the colours, and nothing anywhere says so: no warning, no error, and the generated image looks deliberate. Proven live on 2026-07-19: gamesdesign.co.uk's content_hero guide specifies 'cyan #00bcd4 on near-black #121212', and the stored assets.origin_prompt for content_hero_tool_ehp_calculator ends at 'colour palette: near-black ground (#121212).' — the cyan never reached the model. The two generated images came back orange/navy and teal, inconsistent with each other, which is exactly the style-drift failure that failed the D13 owner gate in July. This is not a site-config mistake: robot-hands.com, the testbed whose imagery PASSED that gate, composes to 233 chars and is also truncated — it only looks correct because its cut happens to fall AFTER 'electric blue (#0080FF)'. The difference between the fleet's good site and its bad one is where a character count landed. I mitigated in config (terse medium/mood, accent first, bringing three sites to 139-147 chars) and confirmed the fix end-to-end: the regenerated prompt carries the full palette and the regenerated images are correctly cyan-on-near-black and consistent with each other. But config phrasing discipline is not a fix — the next site with an expressive medium silently loses its colours again. This plan makes the palette structurally survivable. It deliberately does NOT raise the cap; see risks.

=== ROUNDS 2-4, in brief (each answered and earned approvals): blast radius enumerated (8 directions carry a palette, 5 lose it today, 8/8 keep it after); remediation population exact (robot-hands' 6 content_hero assets; A6.5 path; 3 of 6 wait out the bugs_open/020 owner hold); callers enumerated; SafeCut extracted rather than a second hand-rolled truncation. Round-4 lows are answered inside the edits: TruncateString's 31 call sites enumerated (edit 4), the clause-order phrasing made precise (edit 1), the 100-char-preview claim quoted verbatim (grounded_in).

=== ROUND 5 — A SELF-CAUGHT CORRECTION. The owner asked for a re-check before commit; I simulated the exact Go truncation against all 8 live directions, and my round-2 claim to the guardian was WRONG: under rounds 2-4's plan robot-hands content_hero keeps ONLY the palette, not 'palette whole minus two mood adjectives'. Mechanism: the backoff cuts at the FIRST '. ' past minKeep (strings.Index). Latent today (short medium leads, first boundary < minKeep, comma branch runs); ARMED by a >100-char palette clause leading — the cut lands at the palette's end and discards medium and mood that would fit. Fix is one word, Index -> LastIndex (keep every complete sentence that fits), plus a fixture that FAILS under Index and passes under LastIndex. Post-fix simulation: all 4 content_hero overrides keep palette+medium; robot-hands drops only its mood. None of the nine round-4 seats caught this — the simulation did, which is why the fixture is in the plan.
STATED TRADE previous rounds under-stated: the four BASE voices (304-398 chars) cannot fit palette AND prose in 200 regardless of order or backoff. Today: prose-without-colours. Under this plan: colours-without-prose. Value choice argued in risks; made visible by the WARN; correctable per site in config, live immediately.
SIZE NOTE: one earlier round was VOIDED by bugs_open/019 (edit-quality hit stop_reason=max_tokens); kept compressed deliberately.

plan.summary: The imagery style guide's palette is composed last and truncated away by a 200-char cap, so brand colours silently never reach the model. Fix: (1) compose the palette FIRST; (2) change the truncation backoff from first-sentence to last-sentence-within-cap — without this, the reorder ARMS a latent backoff bug that throws away the medium too (found by simulating the fleet's 8 live directions; the round-2 claim about robot-hands was wrong); (3) make truncation loud; (4) single rune-safe cut primitive shared with TruncateString, which carries the same byte-slice defect. Adds the missing test coverage, driving the real composition function.

edits.rationale: Palette is the shortest field and the one carrying brand identity; medium and mood are prose and degrade gracefully when clipped. Ordering it first makes truncation lose the expendable half. PRECISION (round 5, editquality): clause ORDER changes unconditionally for every direction — 'no behavioural change under the cap' means no INFORMATION change (same clauses, all present); whether order itself affects model output is the unmeasured variable already carried in risks (c), observed at the landing gate.

edits.rationale: Three changes, one file. (a) SafeCut delegation (edit 4) — one truncation algorithm in the tree. (b) ROUND 5, THE SUBSTANTIVE CORRECTION, self-caught when the owner asked for a re-check before commit: the backoff cuts at the FIRST '. ' past minKeep (strings.Index). Today that is latent — the short medium leads, so the first boundary lands before minKeep and the comma branch runs. Once a >100-char palette clause leads, the first-sentence branch ALWAYS fires at the end of the palette and discards medium AND mood that would have fit. Simulated against all 8 live fleet directions: under round 4's plan, robot-hands content_hero kept ONLY the palette — my round-2 claim to the guardian ('loses two mood adjectives') was FALSE. Index -> LastIndex keeps every complete sentence that fits (strictly ≥ content, still whole sentences): robot-hands content_hero then keeps palette + medium, dropping only the mood — which is what I had wrongly claimed before. (c) The WARN: the existing log previews 100 chars against a 200-char cap, so it structurally cannot show a loss. New field is additive (`truncated` bool); nothing renamed or removed.

Drives the REAL composition function (round 3's objection) with the robot-hands-shaped fixture whose palette clause exceeds minKeep — the case that distinguishes Index from LastIndex: under Index the medium assertion FAILS (palette-only), under LastIndex it passes. Asserts all three survival properties: palette, medium, and the subject never truncated. Coverage absence evidenced: grep for these symbols across platform/orchestration/actions/*_test.go returns 0 hits.

ROUND 4 answering reuse_agent; ROUND 5 adds the caller enumeration guardian asked for. datahelpers.TruncateString is `s[:maxLength] + "..."` — a raw byte slice with the identical rune defect. CALLERS, enumerated by grep (31 call sites, 7 files, ALL in platform/orchestration/actions/): ai_actions.go (10), generate_image_actions.go (9), feed_actions.go (4), component_library.go (3), git_deployer_actions.go (2), feed_triage_actions.go (2), research_actions.go (1). Every call site is a log/preview or prompt-preview truncation; none feeds a byte-exact contract (each already appends '...', so exact-length callers could not exist). Signature and ellipsis unchanged — behavioural delta is at most 3 bytes shorter output when the cut lands mid-rune, in exchange for never emitting invalid UTF-8. Expressing TruncateString via SafeCut leaves one truncation algorithm in the package.

plan.risks: Below the cap, identical output apart from clause order. Above it, prompts change materially — the point. THE BASE-VOICE TRADE, stated plainly: all four base voices exceed the cap so much that palette and prose cannot both fit; today they ship prose-without-colours, under this plan colours-without-prose. Why palette wins the tie: colour is the field owners actually pin (design_intent.palette.reference_values; the colour-churn landmine), while planner-emitted subject prompts frequently restate medium in-line, and the WARN now names every site still over cap so the config remedy (shorten the palette gloss — hex codes need no prose) is applied deliberately, not by luck. I will shorten the three base guides I authored (config, live immediately); robot-hands' base guide predates me and is FLAGGED to the owner, not silently edited. Edit 4 widens blast radius beyond imagery only by making TruncateString's existing byte slice rune-safe; signature and ellipsis unchanged. DELIBERATELY NOT PROPOSED: raising the cap (needs provider knowledge in the action layer — the documented drift class; a provider-aware direction budget belongs in the ADAPTER next to bugs_open/028's fold, noted as future work, not smuggled in here). LANDING GATE: (a) regenerate robot-hands' 3 ARTICLE content heroes, re-check against D13 criteria (its 3 TOOL heroes wait out the bugs_open/020 owner hold); (b) confirm live via the new WARN firing for an over-cap site — a genuinely new format string cannot come from a stale same-tag binary, which is A6.3's actual requirement; symbol greps are unvalidated markers there; (c) observe >=5 generations in the same roll window as 028's fold, attributing changes carefully. If (a) regresses, fix that site's CONFIG; do not revert the reorder — 5 of 8 directions lose their palette today.
